precepts.text: I know that my redeemer liveth and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth; and though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God, whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another.
precepts.point: Jeremiah 46:27: fear not, O my servant Jacob, because Jacob's trouble and Armageddon are coming; I will save thee from afar off, this far-off land, and thy seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest and at ease, and none shall make him afraid.
precepts.why:
Isaiah 33:17 says “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty”, and Job shows how. “For I know that my redeemer liveth”. Our redeemer is Christ, who sacrificed himself for our people, the twelve tribes of Israel. “and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth”: in the latter day our redeemer shall stand upon the earth.

“And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God”. Job said, after my death, when worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God. He knew he would be resurrected, regenerated, and we have to know that thing too. Although you die, you are going to be resurrected and regenerated, and that is when your eyes shall see the King in his beauty.

“Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another”. It is not going to be somebody else, and it is not only spiritual, as the Christians say, because Christians don't know the Bible. Job said, I'm going to be back for myself, and I'm going to behold the Lord with my own eyes, and not another, “though my reins be consumed within me”: though my body be destroyed.

precepts.text: All my inward friends abhorred me, and they whom I loved are turned against me.
precepts.point: They have taught their tongue to speak lies. Some brethren online slander the bishops, deacons and captains every chance they get.
precepts.why:
“Take ye heed every one of his neighbour, and trust ye not in any brother: for every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders.” To supplant is to betray, to plot. Job knew what it is to be betrayed by those closest to him: “All my inward friends abhorred me: and they whom I loved are turned against me.”

That is how Maduro was taken in Venezuela. It was betrayal from within. His own elite bodyguards, handpicked for their loyalty and trained to take a bullet for him, took American money instead. The outer guards were told to stand down, the cameras and alarms were disabled, and the last two bodyguards surrendered without firing a single shot. The same thing happened to Jovenel in Haiti. Those were our people, the northern kingdom, and they handed him over. And Esau planned it for more than a year, studying who could be turned: one with a sick daughter, one bitter that others were promoted over him, one disillusioned.

The same spirit is among us. Other Israelite camps want to destroy IUIC by slandering the members and the leadership, because black people will believe anything without proof. They slander the Bishop, the deacons and the captains every chance they get, and then come to the door asking to fellowship. We are good. We don't believe the same thing, and we will never come together with them.

And inside: the brother who says, why is he a captain, I know more scripture than him, why do the young men always travel with the Bishop? Maybe the young men are thirstier for the word than you. They know they don't know everything; you think you know it all. Fix that spirit, or you will be the next traitor, the inward friend turned against those who loved him. God hates a traitor.

precepts.text: Job shall see his redeemer for himself and his eyes shall behold him; Balaam shall behold him, but not nigh.
precepts.point: There shall come a Star out of Jacob: the Star is Christ, the root and offspring of David, the bright and morning star. And a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel: the sceptre belongs to kings, so the prophecy is that the King shall rise out of Israel.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

precepts.why:
“I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh.” Balaam is saying the Most High will raise him up again in the last days, but as a servant, far off from the King; he will behold him, but he will not be near him.

Compare that with Job. “For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth: And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God: Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another; though my reins be consumed within me.”

Job shall see his redeemer for himself and his own eyes shall behold Him; Balaam shall behold Him, but not nigh. The contrast shows Job was an Israelite and not of another nation. Balaam has no such nearness, because the redeemer is not his.

precepts.text: In the regeneration the Son of man sits in the throne of his glory and the servants judge the tribes of Israel, which is the day Job looks to.
precepts.point: Verses 25 through 27 are going into the regeneration; when you go back and read them, this is Job looking past the grave to seeing God for himself in a resurrected body.

note.label: Job 19: I Know That My Redeemer Liveth

precepts.why:
“Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.” In the regeneration the Son of man sits in the throne of his glory and the servants judge the tribes of Israel. That is the day Job looks to.

Verses 25 through 27 are going into the regeneration: “I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth: And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God”. When you go back and read them, this is Job looking past the grave to seeing God for himself in a resurrected body, “Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another”. That is why he wanted his words written, printed in a book, graven with an iron pen and lead in the rock forever, so that this testimony would stand.

points: Oh that my words were now written! oh that they were printed in a book! And they are now.
For I know that my redeemer liveth: the redeemer is Christ. And that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth: Christ shall stand on the earth in the latter days.
Job understood regeneration. He knew that Christ would return in the latter days and that Job would be back to see him for himself. Who Job is today, we do not know; the Lord knows.

And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God: that is regeneration. Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another: my spirit is not going to be in another person's body; my own eyes will look upon the redeemer.
Job answers and asks how long they will vex his soul and break him in pieces with words, saying they have reproached him ten times and are not ashamed.

note.label: Job 19: I Know That My Redeemer Liveth

points: He grants that if indeed he has erred, his error remains with himself, but tells them that God has overthrown him and compassed him with his net.

note.label: Job 19: I Know That My Redeemer Liveth

points: Job cries out of wrong and is not heard, and there is no judgment, for God has fenced up his way and set darkness in his paths.

note.label: Job 19: I Know That My Redeemer Liveth

points: God has stripped him of his glory, taken the crown from his head, destroyed him on every side, and removed his hope like a tree that is pulled up.

note.label: Job 19: I Know That My Redeemer Liveth

points: God's troops come together and raise up their way against him and camp round about his tabernacle, so Job feels himself besieged by the hand of the Most High.

note.label: Job 19: I Know That My Redeemer Liveth

points: Job's brethren are put far from him, his acquaintance are estranged, his kinsfolk have failed, and his familiar friends have forgotten him.

note.label: Job 19: I Know That My Redeemer Liveth

points: He is an alien in the sight of his own household, his servant gives him no answer, and his breath is strange to his wife.

note.label: Job 19: I Know That My Redeemer Liveth

points: Even young children despise him and those he loved are turned against him, so he pleads, Have pity upon me, O ye my friends, for the hand of God hath touched me.

note.label: Job 19: I Know That My Redeemer Liveth

points: Job wishes his words were written and printed in a book, graven with an iron pen and lead in the rock forever, so that this testimony would stand.

note.label: Job 19: I Know That My Redeemer Liveth

points: He declares that he knows his Redeemer liveth and shall stand at the latter day upon the earth, and that though worms destroy his body, yet in his flesh shall he see God.
Verses 25 through 27 are going into the regeneration; when you go back and read them, this is Job looking past the grave to seeing God for himself in a resurrected body.

note.label: Job 19: I Know That My Redeemer Liveth

points: Job warns his friends that if they say the root of the matter is found in him and keep persecuting him, they should be afraid of the sword themselves.

note.label: Job 19: I Know That My Redeemer Liveth

points: The wrath brings the punishments of the sword, that they may know there is a judgment, so Job turns their own accusation back on them.
